title: Angel One Ltd - 543235 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Angel One Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25.4% YoY to ₹14.3 billion and PAT rose 102.1% YoY to ₹2.3 billion, while sequential revenue slipped 2.3%.
summary.overview: Gross revenue reached ₹14.3 billion (+25.4% YoY, -2.3% QoQ) as industry trading softened, mainly on lower derivative volumes across 406 million orders. Reported EBDAT was ₹3.6 billion (32.7% margin), and management said normalized EBDAT margin was 43.6% versus 44.4% last quarter after adjusting for IPL spend, increments, variable pay and fresh ESOP grants. Interest income rose 2.6% QoQ to ₹4.7 billion, with the period-end client funding book at a record ₹71.5 billion. Credit distribution grew 130% YoY to ₹5.3 billion, but management did not explain the quarter-on-quarter softness in disbursals that analysts raised.

segments.name: Broking (core trading platform)
segments.commentary: Contributes close to 60% of gross revenue and is the largest acquisition engine. Turnover market share was 22.2% in equity derivatives, 17.4% in cash equities and 20.2% in overall retail equity turnover.

segments.name: Client funding (MTF)
segments.commentary: Interest income ₹4.7 billion, 32.6% of gross revenue. Average book ₹61.4 billion and period-end book ₹71.5 billion; 83% of exposure is below ₹100,000 per client.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: About 3% of revenue and moderated QoQ on seasonally weaker insurance sales and muted credit disbursement. Lending is run through 7 lending partners.

segments.name: Wealth management (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: Wealth-tech AUM crossed ₹32.3 billion; UHNI AUM ₹87.3 billion across 263 families; total wealth AUM ₹134.4 billion (+33.3%). Revenue not disclosed; burn about 4% of consolidated operating margin for AMC and wealth combined this quarter.

segments.name: Asset management (AMC)
segments.commentary: AUM crossed ₹6.2 billion. Currently passive-only; product rollout mostly happened in the last quarter of FY26, and management said it is evaluating an expanded product suite.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated a 45% to 50% margin guidance on an adjusted basis, with the 40% to 45% standalone range referenced in analyst questions; it said the guidance is intact.
Employee cost for FY27 expected at about ₹11 billion, including stock option cost, in line with FY26.
AMC and wealth burn expected at about 3% to 3.5% of operating margin for the full year, versus about 4% this quarter.
Wealth and AMC businesses expected to break even incrementally in about 3 to 4 years.
First interim dividend of ₹1 per share approved, record date July 21, 2026.
Lending expected to rise from a small base; management declined to give quarterly targets. AMC expansion details to come over the next 2 to 3 quarters.
Management said it is not commenting on July activity: about 15 days of data, and it said nothing fundamental has changed for broking volumes over a 12-month horizon.
capex_capacity: Loan against securities (LAS) is in a small pilot, currently in controlled-pilot mode, with infrastructure built; management expects the business to become large over the next 2 to 3 quarters once customer experience data is available.
Active assisted partners (APs) about 9,800, roughly 10,000 per management; plans to reinstate mutual fund distributor acquisition and multiproduct selling.
US equities: GIFT City licence obtained; existing offerings are being upgraded and the product is not yet launched, so no pricing was disclosed.
Ask Angel AI assistant serving over 1.1 million users; AI is used across onboarding, grievance automation and analytics.
Wealth model: RM productivity and automation are being used to lower the cost to serve; the second wealth business (₹1 crore to ₹50 crore net worth) is about ₹3,400–3,500 crore AUM.
demand_pricing: Industry volumes moderated sequentially; Angel One said its order decline mirrored industry trends, with lower derivative volumes the main driver.

Cash realization per order rose QoQ on a mix shift (orders above vs below ₹20,000) and on a value-added plan for assisted clients. A November pricing change also contributed. Management said it would not bake in further increases.
Client acquisition cost rose in the IPL period. Management said total acquisition cost (not per-client CAC) is moving with market conditions.
Nifty active client base softened and CDSL-reported client acquisition was softer in recent months, per management.
Average client funding book grew to ₹61.4 billion, while the period-end book reached a record ₹71.5 billion.
Lending: 7 lending partners, mostly banks and large NBFCs, with a couple of fintechs added in the last 2 to 3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why has credit disbursement declined over recent quarters (about ₹710 crore at Q3, ₹610 crore, then ₹530 crore), and what has not worked?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh Agarwal cited customer sentiment, lender underwriting and pricing, and platform friction as causes. Management said lenders are recalibrating risk and pricing, and that some funnel friction is being fixed. It maintained that the long-term thesis is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How is broking trending in July after a weak start, and how should the next quarters look?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said only about 15 days of July were available, so there is too early a read. He said nothing fundamental had changed and that the company does not comment on mid-quarter volumes or MTF run rates.

qa_highlights.question: Wealth management revenue, cost and breakeven plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet Agrawal said wealth and AMC revenue are not disclosed. Burn is about 4% of operating margin this quarter, expected at 3% to 3.5% for FY27, with incremental breakeven in about 3 to 4 years. No absolute quantum was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AMC's AUM still small after launch, and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Majumdar said the AMC has been passive-only for about 15 months, with most products launched in the last quarter of FY26. Management expects clearer strategy visibility over the next 3 to 4 quarters and declined to give AUM targets.

qa_highlights.question: Client funding risk if markets fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said risk is limited because margins follow exchange-prescribed levels and sometimes exceed them. Vineet Agrawal added that the company has seen no issues in past market shocks and sees low penetration among its clients.

qa_highlights.question: Employee count decline (from about 4,139 at FY25-end to about 3,300 at FY26-end) and cash realization jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a headcount target or divisional breakdown, citing efficiency gains. Cash realization gains were attributed to order-size mix and the value-added assisted plan. It said it would not bake in further gains.

qa_highlights.question: Acquisition cost rising during IPL, and is there a structural increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe said IPL spend is branding, not acquisition cost, and that CAC tends to rise during IPL and then normalize. Long-term equity penetration (5% to 10% of retail wealth) remains the driver.

qa_highlights.question: A retail customer complained about a restricted-basket (RSM) restriction in the app.
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish Kenghe apologised, said the restriction reflects Angel One's own risk policies on top of SEBI rules, and asked the customer to email ceo@angelone.in for an offline follow-up. He did not commit to removing the basket.

risks_watch: Credit disbursal momentum: disbursal values fell QoQ across recent quarters, and management gave no quantified recovery target.
Volume and activity in July 2026 after a soft start; the RBI circular impact on funding is described as transient, with no liquidity issue seen.
Client acquisition cost and active-client trends, with Nifty active clients and CDSL acquisition softer per management.
Wealth and AMC cash burn: about 4% of operating margin this quarter, and breakeven is not due until about 3 to 4 years out.
Regulatory developments, which management described as evolving without giving specifics. Restricted-basket policy raised by a customer on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term opportunity and margin discipline, but evasive on near-term volumes, credit disbursal trends, and wealth and AMC specifics. Management repeatedly declined to comment on July data or disclose segment revenue and CAC, and deflected the credit and AMC questions to longer horizons.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 of this financial year was another quarter of healthy execution for the company.
More importantly, adjusting for these seasonal items, our normalized EBDAT margin stood at 43.6% compared with 44.4% in the previous quarter, remaining comfortably within our guided operating range.
So we don't see any short-term to midterm blip in the credit growth.
I'm very happy about it, but I think feedbacks like this should be considered very seriously.

growth.why: Guidance is limited to reiterated margin band (45-50% adjusted, 40-45% standalone), FY27 employee cost of about ₹11 billion and wealth/AMC burn of 3-3.5%, with no revenue growth target; Q1 revenue rose 25.4% YoY but fell 2.3% QoQ on lower derivative volumes, and July activity was not commented on, so growth outlook is flat.
